title: Vanishing of conditional mutual information for an almost-surely constant variable
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be discrete random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ — where $\mu$ is either the zero measure or a probability measure — taking values in countable measurable spaces $S$, $T$, and $U$ respectively, with each of $X$, $Y$, $Z$ almost surely taking only finitely many values, and with $X$ and $Y$ measurable. If there is a constant $c \in T$ such that $Y = c$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the conditional mutual information satisfies $I[X : Y \mid Z; \mu] = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: μ is zero or a probability measure
X, Y, Z have finite range
Y equals a constant c μ-a.e.
replaced: If $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : T$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = 0$.
